scope.selection: Deterministic midpoint of hard items, midpoint of advanced items, and midpoint lesson in each frozen package.
limitations: A sample review cannot establish the correctness or difficulty calibration of all bank items.
No live infrastructure, model endpoint, distributed cache, browser integration or production ML evaluation was executed for this review.

Difficulty judgments require subject-matter review and eventual learner performance evidence.
No human educational approval or publication approval is inferred.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: A paused worker resumes with lease generation 41 after generation 42 has taken ownership. Both can reach the storage service. Which control prevents generation 41 from committing after the transfer?
options: Serialize queue delivery while allowing both workers to write to storage directly
Enforce generation 42 at storage and reject older generations on every commit
Check generation 41 in worker memory before beginning the next long operation
Renew generation 42 more frequently while accepting writes without generation checks
sampled_formal_items.answer: Enforce generation 42 at storage and reject older generations on every commit
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The revised hard case specifies generations 41 and 42 and a stale writer reaching storage. Only a destination-enforced generation check on commits prevents the obsolete writer; local checks, heartbeat frequency and queue serialization do not fence a previously delivered operation.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: A cache accepts arbitrary tenant and invoice strings, including colons. Concatenating tenant=a,id=bc and tenant=ab,id=c aliases both to abc. Summary and private views must also remain distinct. Which key design prevents both tuple aliasing and cross-view reuse without restricting these strings?
options: Join tenant, id and view with colons and hash the joined string
Serialize [tenant+id,view] and hash the serialized value
Serialize [tenant,id] and let TTL distinguish summary from private
Serialize [tenant,id,view] as a JSON tuple before optional hashing
sampled_formal_items.answer: Serialize [tenant,id,view] as a JSON tuple before optional hashing
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The revised advanced case requires preserving arbitrary string tuple boundaries and a distinct permission-dependent view. JSON tuple encoding preserves all three string dimensions; delimiter joining, concatenation before serialization and omitted view each violate a stated constraint.

sampled_lesson.title: Cache representations with ownership and freshness rules
sampled_lesson.boundary_review: The tuple fixture prints false then true and distinguishes tenant strings for the supplied tuples. It does not implement a cache, permission checks, eviction, distributed locking or a general encoder for arbitrary JavaScript values. The lesson explicitly limits the result to the shown dimensions and inputs.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: A balanced validation set yields high precision, but production prevalence is one percent. Sensitivity is 0.8 and specificity 0.9. Approximate production precision is what?
options: 7.5 percent
80 percent
89 percent
50 percent
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: At prevalence 0.01, TP proportion is 0.8*0.01=0.008 and FP proportion is (1-0.9)*0.99=0.099. Precision is 0.008/(0.008+0.099)=0.074766..., so 7.5 percent is correct.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: Two held-out accounts have true costs $100 and $1000. Model A predicts $100 and $1600; B predicts $200 and $1200. Natural-log RMSE is about 0.33 for A and 0.51 for B. Deployment instead requires minimum weighted currency MAE using weights 1 and 5, and at most $250 absolute error on the high-value account. Which assessment follows that policy?
options: B; weighted MAEs A=$300, B=$150; both satisfy the cap
Neither; weighted MAEs A=$500, B≈$183; both violate the cap
B; weighted MAEs A=$500, B≈$183; only B meets the cap
A; weighted MAEs A=$100, B≈$117; lower log RMSE decides
sampled_formal_items.answer: B; weighted MAEs A=$500, B≈$183; only B meets the cap
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The advanced item now requires computing A=(0+5*600)/6=$500, B=(100+5*200)/6≈$183.33, checking high-value absolute errors $600 versus $200 against the $250 cap, and applying the stated objective despite A having lower log RMSE.

sampled_lesson.title: Distinguish ranking metrics from numeric error
sampled_lesson.boundary_review: MAE([0,0],[0,4]) is 2.0; RMSE is sqrt(8)=2.828427 rounded; all positive ranking scores exceed all negative scores, yielding ROC-AUC 1.0. The fixture uses scikit-learn metrics on supplied data and explicitly does not establish production accuracy, representative sampling, causal impact or business cost acceptability.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: The server stores idempotency keys for one day. A timed-out write is retried after two days and its state is unknown. What assumption is unsafe?
options: The old key still prevents duplicates
A different key can bypass the old deduplication record
Authoritative status can aid recovery
The prior call may already have run
sampled_formal_items.answer: The old key still prevents duplicates
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The ambiguous new logical action phrase is replaced by A different key can bypass the old deduplication record. This states server deduplication behavior without claiming a new key necessarily represents new user intent.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: Two tool calls fail: a quote rejects quantity=7 before execution because its range is 1–5; a shipment times out with unknown commit status under key K. Raw diagnostics contain credentials. Policy allows one argument correction and a status lookup, but no second shipment until reconciliation. Which planner-visible feedback and next action respect all constraints?
options: Expose redacted stack frames and retryable=true for both; replay both calls using their prior keys
Expose only generic failure and mark both calls unexecuted; rerun the original calls without lookup
Expose quantity range and opaque traces; correct once and reconcile shipment K before retrying
Expose quantity range and opaque traces; correct once and resend the shipment under a fresh key
sampled_formal_items.answer: Expose quantity range and opaque traces; correct once and reconcile shipment K before retrying
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The advanced item now distinguishes rejected-before-execution validation from an uncertain committed shipment; the answer must preserve safe feedback, a single bounded quote correction, and reconciliation of shipment K before replay. All alternatives violate at least one explicit constraint.

sampled_lesson.title: Classify tool failures and return actionable safe feedback
sampled_lesson.expected_output:
invalid_arguments False
denied False
temporarily_unavailable True
sampled_lesson.boundary_review: The Python classify function returns a category and a boolean based solely on three supplied category strings. Output is invalid_arguments False, denied False, temporarily_unavailable True. The prose separately discusses timeouts with unknown write status and bounds retries; the example does not execute a model, tool backend, authorization service or retry loop, and explicitly calls itself an offline mock.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: A Terraform 1.9 child uses aws.primary for us-east-1 and aws.replica for eu-west-1. The root configures aws.us in us-east-1 and aws.eu in eu-west-1. Which child declaration and caller mapping satisfy both regional contracts?
options: Declare both child aliases; map primary to aws.us and replica to aws.eu
Declare only the default; map primary to aws.us and replica to aws.eu
Declare both child aliases; map primary to aws.eu and replica to aws.us
Declare both child aliases; pass aws.us only through the default aws name
sampled_formal_items.answer: Declare both child aliases; map primary to aws.us and replica to aws.eu
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The hard item now specifies child aws.primary/aws.replica and root aws.us/aws.eu configurations with required regions. Only declaring both child aliases and mapping the intended regional root configurations meets both contracts.

sampled_formal_items.prompt: A reviewed Terraform apply creates a new database and records its binding in state, then fails updating DNS. Old traffic still reaches the healthy old database. The new database must be preserved, and traffic cannot move before its health is verified. Which recovery sequence respects these constraints?
options: Keep old traffic; verify new DB health and state, then review a non-destructive DNS recovery plan
Keep old traffic; replay the previous saved plan because its earlier policy check approved all actions
Move traffic now; use refresh-only apply to perform the failed DNS update without resource actions
Revert source; approve deletion of the recorded new database because no traffic moved to it
sampled_formal_items.answer: Keep old traffic; verify new DB health and state, then review a non-destructive DNS recovery plan
sampled_formal_items.technical_review: The advanced item now specifies a created database recorded in state, a failed DNS update, healthy old traffic, database retention and a health prerequisite. Correct recovery preserves current service and bindings, verifies health, then reviews a fresh non-destructive DNS recovery plan; stale replay, refresh-only as a DNS writer and source-revert deletion violate specific constraints.

after.prompt: A reviewed Terraform apply creates a new database and records its binding in state, then fails updating DNS. Old traffic still reaches the healthy old database. The new database must be preserved, and traffic cannot move before its health is verified. Which recovery sequence respects these constraints?
options: Keep old traffic; verify new DB health and state, then review a non-destructive DNS recovery plan
Keep old traffic; replay the previous saved plan because its earlier policy check approved all actions
Move traffic now; use refresh-only apply to perform the failed DNS update without resource actions

after.explanation: Partial apply is not atomic rollback: the new database exists and its recorded binding must be preserved. Inspect remote effects and state, verify new database health, and review a fresh non-destructive plan before moving DNS.
